Answer: B
Reason: The CT images demonstrate a peripheral, rounded soft-tissue opacity in the right lower lung that is contiguous with the pleura and associated with volume loss (atelectasis) and pleural effusion/thickening. This appearance, often showing a "comet tail" sign of converging vessels/bronchi on cross-section, is characteristic of rounded atelectasis (folded lung), a benign condition frequently associated with asbestos-related pleural disease.
